newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Reshuffle rumours deter buyers of Russian shares.
newsitem.headline: Reshuffle rumours deter buyers of Russian shares.

text.p: Investors held off buying Russian shares on Wednesday on nervousness about an impending cabinet reshuffle, dealers said.
Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, facing speculation about his own future, on Tuesday promised a major cabinet reshuffle after criticism of the government by President Boris Yeltsin.
The 23-share Russian Trading System index inched up to 328.03 from 327.35 at Tuesday's close.

"The market closed a bit better yesterday but some people are staying away from it now because of the rumours about Chernomyrdin, that Yeltsin might dismiss him," said Peter Kizenko, chief equities trader at ING Barings.
Other dealers said leading shares were easing.
"There's been some profit-taking on LUKoil, Mosenergo and Rostelekom," said Viktor Pitaleff, head trader at Renaissance.

At 1030 GMT Mosenergo had fallen to $1.405 from Tuesday's closing $1.445. Rostelekom recovered from early lows to $3.922 from Tuesday's closing $3.910 and LUKoil recovered from early lows to Tuesday's closing $15.15.
Surgutneftegaz was $0.752, up on Tuesday's closing $0.750 after a fund apparently linked to the group's pension fund won an investment tender for 40 percent of parent Surgut Holding.
Norilsk Nickel eased to $6.90 from $6.95 on reports its main plant may strike next month.
